question: Mechanical thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion ischaemic stroke is effective only within 6 hours of symptom onset; patients presenting beyond 6 hours cannot benefit from thrombectomy.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — false. The standard window is 6 hours, but with perfusion mismatch imaging (CT-perfusion or MRI-DWI/PWI), thrombectomy can be extended to 24 hours in selected patients. The 6-hour limit is not absolute.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: That statement is false. While the standard thrombectomy window is up to 6 hours, select patients with favourable perfusion imaging (evidence of salvageable penumbra — DEFUSE-3 and DAWN trial criteria) can benefit up to 24 hours from last known well.
